title: When Cloud TEEs Encounter Availability: A Lightweight Framework for Verifiable CPU Availability
evidence_span: AvaTEE integrates resource negotiation into remote attestation, then uses a trusted scheduler for runtime monitoring and preemptive arbitration; FPGA evaluation reports protection under contention, less than 2% startup/normal-runtime overhead, and 1.70% average overhead versus Keystone.
problem: Trusted execution environments depend on untrusted schedulers and can suffer CPU denial-of-service attacks that compromise enclave availability.
method_or_artifact: Availability-verifiable remote attestation with resource commitments plus trusted runtime monitoring and preemptive scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: TEE contention and CPU-DoS evaluation on an FPGA, compared with native TEEs and Keystone; enclave workloads, contention levels, FPGA configuration, and attack traces are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: FPGA implementation of a TEE/trusted scheduler and remote-attestation path; TCB, processor, memory, enclave size, and scheduler details are unspecified.
metrics: Native TEE: 94.8% performance loss and up to 19.7x slowdown under contention
Less than 2% enclave startup and normal-runtime overhead
limits: The description omits threat-model detail, enclave workloads, fairness guarantees, hardware cost, and attestation protocol changes.
FPGA results may not transfer to deployed CPU TEEs or cloud scheduling environments.
Official description only; availability and security claims require paper-level verification.

title: Finding Behavior Bugs in IoT Messaging Protocols with Automated Oracle Generation and Monitoring
evidence_span: ARES extracts executable behavior oracles from protocol specifications and applies LLM-driven behavior filtering for real-time compliance monitoring; evaluation across six IoT protocol implementations reports 25 new bugs at 87.5% precision, including 21 behavior bugs, with 18 confirmed or fixed and 10 CVEs assigned.
problem: IoT messaging implementations can violate protocol behavior specifications in ways that enable unauthorized access or device compromise, while manual oracle construction is incomplete.
method_or_artifact: Automated specification-to-executable-oracle extraction with LLM-assisted behavior filtering and runtime monitoring.
workload_or_benchmark: Six widely used IoT messaging protocol implementations; protocol names, test volume, oracle coverage, and precision denominator are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: IoT protocol implementations and monitoring environment; device platforms, network conditions, specification formats, and LLM model/configuration are unspecified.
baselines: manual or existing protocol bug-detection workflows
limits: The description omits recall, oracle completeness, false negatives, test budget, protocol distribution, and independent confirmation criteria.
CVE assignment and fixes indicate impact for a subset, not prevalence across IoT deployments.
Official description only; security findings require reproducible disclosure and paper-level verification.

title: Cell-Structure-Independent Transistor-Level Placement and MOL-Aware Routing Framework Beyond the Standard-Cell Paradigm
evidence_span: The framework directly places transistors on the design canvas and couples cell-structure-independent placement with middle-of-line-aware routing; experiments report considerable wirelength and area improvements against a commercial standard-cell tool and state-of-the-art transistor-level work, without numeric values.
problem: Fixed standard-cell boundaries constrain pin access, M0/MOL routing, wirelength, and area optimization at advanced technology nodes.
method_or_artifact: Transistor-level placement independent of fixed cell structure coupled to an MOL-aware routing engine.
workload_or_benchmark: VLSI designs evaluated against a commercial standard-cell flow and prior transistor-level work; circuit suite, technology node, timing/power constraints, and metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Advanced-node transistor-level physical design with dense pin access and MOL/M0 routing resources; PDK, design rules, extraction, and signoff assumptions are unspecified.
limits: The description omits numeric PPA results, timing/power impacts, routability, design-rule compliance, and technology-node details.
Relaxing cell structure may increase design complexity, variability, and verification/signoff cost.
Official description only; physical-design claims require paper-level and signoff-condition verification.

title: SSD Reforge: Dynamic Parity Management to Extend SSD Lifetime Under Aging
evidence_span: SSD Reforge models RBER-based error probability, solves parity stripe grouping, and uses Reliability-Aware Striping plus Stripe UPER Leveling for subsequent writes; FEMU experiments with real I/O traces report up to 40% average user-TBW improvement over traditional mode at the lifetime limit.
problem: Flash aging raises raw bit-error rates and limits SSD lifetime by total bytes written or program/erase cycles.
method_or_artifact: Dynamic intra-device parity strengthening with RBER-aware stripe grouping and continued leveling under subsequent writes.
workload_or_benchmark: FEMU SSD simulation evaluated with real I/O traces against traditional protection mode; NAND geometry, trace set, ECC baseline, and lifetime model are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Aging flash SSD with intra-device parity, RBER estimation, and controller-managed striping; NAND generation, channels, ECC, overprovisioning, and latency/energy costs are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 40% average user-TBW increase at the lifetime limit
limits: The description omits latency, write amplification, capacity overhead, energy, trace diversity, and error-model calibration.
Lifetime gains depend on aging distribution, parity budget, workload write pattern, and controller implementation.
Official description only; endurance and performance claims require trace- and device-level verification.

title: A Correlation-Aware GKP Decoder for Fault-Tolerant Continuous-Variable Photonic Quantum Computers
evidence_span: The proposed accelerator implements correlation-aware Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill decoding for continuous-variable photonic quantum computing; 7-nm FinFET synthesis reports 12.96 ns decoding latency, with design-space exploration of accuracy, latency, and area tradeoffs.
problem: Correlation-aware GKP decoding improves error correction but straightforward hardware implementations are too computationally slow for optical-clock operation in tens of nanoseconds.
method_or_artifact: Low-latency hardware accelerator optimized for correlation-aware GKP decoding with synthesis-based design-space exploration.
workload_or_benchmark: Correlation-aware GKP decoding workloads for fault-tolerant continuous-variable photonic quantum computers; decoder sizes, noise model, accuracy target, and comparison architecture are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 7-nm FinFET synthesized decoder intended to meet photonic optical-clock timing; process libraries, frequency assumptions, area, power, and interconnect are unspecified.
baselines: straightforward hardware implementation of correlation-aware decoding
uncorrelated or prior GKP decoding methods
metrics: 12.96 ns decoding latency in 7-nm FinFET synthesis
limits: The description omits decoding accuracy, area, power, throughput, noise assumptions, and baseline latency.
Synthesis timing does not establish post-layout or integrated photonic-system performance.
Official description only; quantum-error-correction and hardware claims require paper-level verification.
